newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia VNK oil company wants bigger refinery stake.
newsitem.headline: Russia VNK oil company wants bigger refinery stake.

text.p: Russia's Eastern Oil Company (VNK) will back a credit from International Moscow Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to Achinsk refinery in exchange for control of the refinery, a VNK official said on Monday.
OAO Vostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya already has a 44.6 percent stake in the refinery, Boris Ivanov, deputy director for securities, told Reuters.

"We shall suggest that Achinsk refinery increase its authorised capital by issuing new shares and then transfer the missing 5.5 percent of shares to us in trust for the period of repaying the credit," Ivanov said.
"If Achinsk refinery refuses, we shall only be able to guarantee the repayment of part of the credit in the amount of our participation in the refinery."
Ivanov said the banks planned to grant a $62 million credit to the refinery and it would have to repay over $100 million in credit and interest payments over six years.
He said Achinsk refinery would discuss the issue at a shareholders' meeting on Agust 15.
VNK, a vertically integrated oil group whose main production unit is Tomskneft, is slated for privatisation by September.
A VNK spokesman said the refinery needed funds to complete a $92.9 million restructuring programme started in 1992.
"Due to the lack of funds for modernisation management of the plant has applied for help to EBRD and the bank asked for a guarantee from VNK as main shareholder," the spokesman said.
VNK's authorised capital is 3.01 billion roubles ($520.22 million). Russia's Tokobank owns 5.2 percent of shares.

Achinsky Neftepererabatyvayushchy Zavod refinery's authorised capital is 512.79 million roubles. Gamma Limited from Vladivostok owns 10 percent of shares, the Krasnoyarsk administration owns 6.24 percent and international investment bank CS First Boston 4.9 percent.
